answer: Agents are paid per surviving channel slot, not per key. A rotating beacon stamps each contention window, and the aggregator meters how many proofs one physical uplink returns in it. A thousand clones on one host finish no faster than a single honest agent, since they share the same bus and radio time, so payout per clone falls toward zero as the farm grows: attacker cost rises with the square of headcount. Admission also needs a timing signature no existing vertex in the channel graph holds, so duplicates are refused. A sybil crowd becomes a narrow lagoon whose members starve each other.
